paper.title_en: Evidence of Higgs Boson Inclusive Production at High Transverse Momentum Decaying to a Pair of <math display="inline"><mi>b</mi></math>-Quarks with the ATLAS Detector
paper.abstract_en: This Letter reports on the first evidence of inclusive Higgs-boson production at high transverse momentum in the <math display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mrow></mover></mrow></math> final state, reconstructed in a single large-radius jet. The results are based on proton-proton collision data recorded by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider at a center-of-mass energies of 13 and 13.6 TeV, corresponding to a total integrated luminosity of <math display="inline"><mrow><mn>301</mn><mtext> </mtext><mtext> </mtext><msup><mrow><mi>fb</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. The study profits from the large background suppression provided by the use of a new transformer-based algorithm for jet identification and the sharper mass and transverse momentum, <math display="inline"><msub><mi>p</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msub></math>, resolution from a dedicated regression model. The yield relative to the standard model prediction for Higgs bosons produced at <math display="inline"><msub><mi>p</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msub></math> larger than 450 GeV is measured to be <math display="inline"><mrow><mn>1.53</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.2</mn><msubsup><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>0.27</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.33</mn></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>±</mo></mrow><mn>0.17</mn></mrow></math>, where the first uncertainty is statistical, the second is experimental systematic, and the third accounts for theory systematic, corresponding to an observed (expected) significance of <math display="inline"><mn>3.8</mn><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2.5</mn><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> relative to the background-only hypothesis. Results are also obtained in three Higgs boson <math display="inline"><msub><mi>p</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msub></math> intervals and found to be compatible with standard model predictions, where the first uncertainty is statistical, the second is experimental systematic, and the third accounts for theory systematic.
authors: De Sousa, M.J. Da Cunha Sargedas
